STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, rim band, flat centre, no inner wall visible).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. The plate looks medium-large relative to the food, so I estimate about 25 cm.
b) Reference: the avocado wedges are roughly 8-9 cm long. The plate spans about 3 avocado-wedge lengths across the long edge, giving about 25-27 cm.
Reconciled width: about 26 cm (square, area ≈ 676 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Cauliflower florets (roasted, with light oil/seasoning): covers roughly 25% of the plate in the upper-left/centre cluster, about 170 cm². Florets are chunky, so the pile is about 2 florets deep at the thickest point, ~3 cm at the peak, averaging ~1.5 cm. Volume ≈ 170 × 1.5 = 255 ml × 0.6 (chopped vegetable) ≈ 153 g.
- Avocado wedges: 3 wedges, each roughly 8 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm-ish thick wedge, about 40-45 g each as a fleshy wedge. Estimate ≈ 3 × 40 = 120 g (mostly flesh; the portion is about 100-130 g).

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no clear base layer under the cauliflower; the plate surface is visible, so no extra items added.

STEP 5 - Energy:
- Roasted cauliflower with light oil: ~50 kcal/100 g (oil adds some fat; estimate 60 kcal/100 g to account for oil).
- Avocado: ~160 kcal/100 g.

Totals: cauliflower 153 g × 0.6 ≈ 92 kcal; avocado 120 g × 1.6 ≈ 192 kcal. Total ≈ 285 kcal, about 273 g of food.
